selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What did the traveler notice about believers and many Sufis?
questions.answer: They often say words that remind people Allah is One.

questions.question: Which group is specially mentioned along with the people of faith?
questions.answer: People connected to a Sufi path.

questions.question: Why did the traveler open a new “door” in his learning journey?
questions.answer: He wanted to move to a higher degree of understanding.

questions.question: What kind of knowledge is not enough in this passage?
questions.answer: A knowledge that is only in the imagination.

questions.question: Why did the traveler want another stopping-place?
questions.answer: He wanted to grow more in understanding.

questions.question: What four heart actions are part of true tawhid in the passage?
questions.answer: Judging, confirming, agreeing, and accepting.

questions.question: When someone sees the world rightly, what do things become?
questions.answer: They become signs that lead to Allah.

questions.question: What does such a person feel about Allah’s nearness?
questions.answer: He feels his Lord is present and not far away.

questions.question: What did the traveler say to his own self before moving on?
questions.answer: He told himself to go forward.

questions.question: What did he witness there that supported tawhid?
questions.answer: Five clear truths over the whole universe.

questions.question: Why did the traveler pay attention to the way people of faith speak?
questions.answer: Because their words gave him a clue about Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What kind of act is remembering Allah’s oneness called in the passage?
questions.answer: It is called a holy duty and an act of worship.

questions.question: What was the traveler hoping to gain by going farther?
questions.answer: A higher and truer level of knowing Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Name another way it describes it.
questions.answer: It is valuable and worship.

questions.question: What kind of understanding was accepted?
questions.answer: One that comes from proof and sure knowledge.

questions.question: In this passage, what is true belief in Allah’s oneness like?
questions.answer: It means truly accepting that Allah is near and can be found with all things.

questions.question: How does a person with true tawhid look at the world?
questions.answer: He sees Allah’s signs everywhere.

questions.question: If someone misses this truth, what hard thing might he think he has to do?
questions.answer: He might think he must remove the world to find Allah.

questions.question: Where did the traveler enter after calling himself onward?
questions.answer: He entered a place about Allah’s actions and making things.

questions.question: What final discovery did the traveler make in that place?
questions.answer: He saw five broad truths that clearly proved Allah is One.

questions.question: What lesson did the traveler learn from the people who often remember Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: He learned that tawhid is deep and has many stages.

questions.question: How does the passage describe this remembrance as an action?
questions.answer: It is worship and a blessed job of the soul.

questions.question: Name one way the passage describes this remembrance.
questions.answer: It is joyful.

questions.question: What habit of believers made the traveler think more deeply?
questions.answer: Their constant saying of words about Allah being One.
